verdict.rationale: iTerm2's GitHub README documents a built-in LLM chat window that can link to sessions and 'run commands on your behalf'. This ships through an optional first-party AI plugin, and community reports describe the Codecierge toolbox and AI-generated commands (e.g. an awk one-liner) in real use. The evidence does not show an agent that plans multi-step tasks or an explicit per-command approval step, so only part of the story is delivered. Missing for 10: documented multi-step task planning, an explicit approval/confirmation flow before execution, in-depth first-party docs on agent behavior.
